text:
Pest: P001
Topic: Identification
Fact: The rice stem borer documented by TNAU is Scirpophaga incertulas.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Stem borer.

Pest: P001
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Stem borer larvae can enter the rice stem and cause drying of the central shoot, known as dead heart; at the ear-bearing stage affected panicles may appear as white ears with chaffy grains.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Stem borer.

Pest: P002
Topic: Identification
Fact: The brown planthopper is identified as Nilaparvata lugens.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Brown plant hopper.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Brown plant hopper.

text:
Pest: P002
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Brown planthopper nymphs and adults feed on plant sap near the base of rice plants; infestation can produce yellowing, browning and drying known as hopper burn.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Brown plant hopper.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Brown plant hopper.

text:
Pest: P003
Topic: Identification
Fact: The white-backed planthopper is identified as Sogatella furcifera.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — White backed plant hopper.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — White backed plant hopper.

text:
Pest: P003
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: White-backed planthopper nymphs and adults suck phloem sap and can cause reduced vigour, stunting, yellowing and hopper-burn symptoms in rice.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — White backed plant hopper.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — White backed plant hopper.

text:
Pest: P004
Topic: Identification
Fact: The rice leaf folder documented by TNAU is Cnaphalocrocis medinalis.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Leaf folder.

Pest: P004
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Rice leaf-folder larvae fold or roll rice leaves and scrape the green tissues; severe infestation can give fields a whitish scorched appearance.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Leaf folder.

Pest: P005
Topic: Identification
Fact: The rice gall midge is identified as Orseolia oryzae.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Gall midge.

Pest: P005
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Gall midge infestation can produce a characteristic silver shoot or onion-leaf symptom and a tubular gall at the base of an affected rice tiller.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Gall midge.

Pest: P006
Topic: Identification
Fact: Rice hispa is identified as Dicladispa armigera.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice Hispa.

Pest: P006
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Rice hispa adults scrape the green tissue of rice leaves while grubs mine within the leaf tissue, producing white streaks or translucent patches.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice Hispa.

Pest: P007
Topic: Identification
Fact: The rice earhead bug documented by TNAU is Leptocorisa acuta.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Ear head bug.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Ear head bug.

text:
Pest: P007
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Rice earhead bugs feed on developing rice grains during the milky stage; feeding can produce discoloured patches and chaffy grains.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Ear head bug.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Ear head bug.

text:
Pest: P008
Topic: Identification
Fact: Rice caseworm is identified as Nymphula depunctalis.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice case worm.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice case worm.

text:
Pest: P008
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Rice caseworm larvae feed on green leaf tissue and make tubular cases from cut leaf portions; these cases may float on the water surface around rice tillers.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice case worm.
citation: TNAU Crop Protection — Rice case worm.

text:
Pest: P009
Topic: Damage symptoms
Fact: Rice thrips damage tender leaves by lacerating leaf tissue and sucking plant sap, producing yellowish or silvery streaks on young rice seedlings.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Thrips.

Pest: P009
Topic: Crop stage / severity
Fact: Rice thrips can affect both nursery and main-field rice, with damage described as more severe under water-stress conditions.
Geographic scope: India / rice production
Source: TNAU Crop Protection — Thrips.
